title: por or para?
intro: Both can mean "for", but they're used differently.
*Para*: where you're going, what for, who it's for, a deadline. *Vou para Lisboa*. *Estudo para aprender*. *É para ti*. *É para amanhã*.
Por: through or along, the reason, an exchange or price, "by" someone, "per". *Passei pelo parque*. Obrigado *pela ajuda*. *Paguei dez* euros *por isto*. *Três vezes por semana*.
notes: *Ir para* suggests going somewhere to stay a while (*Vou para casa*); *ir* a is a shorter visit (*Vou ao supermercado*).

drills.en: I'm going home.
Thanks for everything!
This present is for you.
We went through the park.
I study in order to learn.
I paid ten euros for this book.
I go to the gym three times a week.
The work is due tomorrow.
The book was written by Saramago.
Thanks for the help.
We're leaving for Faro tomorrow.
I stayed at home because of the rain.

title: que, quem, onde, o que
intro: Que is the all-purpose "who", "which" or "that": O *homem que mora aqui*. O *livro que li*.
*Quem* is "who" after a small word like com or de, or "whoever": A *pessoa com quem falei*. *Quem quiser pode vir*.
*Onde* = where: A *cidade onde nasci*. O que = what, "the thing that": *Não percebi o que disseste*.
Cujo = whose. It's mostly written, so just recognise it: O autor cujo *livro li* (the author whose book I read).

examples.pt: O homem que mora aqui é médico.
examples.en: The man who lives here is a doctor.

examples.pt: A pessoa com quem falei foi simpática.
examples.en: The person I spoke to was nice.

examples.pt: Esta é a cidade onde nasci.
examples.en: This is the city where I was born.
I didn't understand what you said.

notes: English often drops "that" (the book I read). Portuguese never drops que: o *livro que li*.
The small word goes in front: a *pessoa com quem falei*, never "*quem falei* com".
*Quem quiser pode vir* = Whoever wants can come (with the future subjunctive).

drills.en: The man who lives here is a doctor.

drills.hint: that, often left out in English
drills.en: The book I read was great.
The person I spoke to was nice.
This is the city where I was born.
I didn't understand what you said.
Whoever wants to can come.
I didn't understand what you said.

drills.answer: Esta é a cidade onde nasci.
drills.en: This is the city where I was born.
The book I bought is expensive.
The friend I told you about arrives today.
drills.why: A person after a small word like de: *quem*.

drills.en: Do what you want.
The house where I live is small.

title: porque, por isso, embora
intro: Words that join ideas: *porque* (because), *por isso* (so, that's why), *mas* (but), *então* (so, then), *embora* (although, with the subjunctive), *apesar* de (despite, with an infinitive or a noun), *enquanto* (while).
To ask why, Portugal usually says *Porque é* que…? On its own or at the end of a question, it's *porquê*, with an accent: *Porquê*? *Estás triste porquê*?

examples.pt: Fiquei em casa porque estava a chover.
examples.en: I stayed at home because it was raining.

examples.pt: Estava a chover, por isso fiquei em casa.
examples.en: It was raining, so I stayed at home.
Although I was tired, I went.

notes: *Apesar* de takes an infinitive, and the personal infinitive works too: *apesar* de estarmos cansados.
*Aliás* (in fact, actually) is very common in conversation.

drills.en: I stayed at home because it was raining.
It was raining, so I stayed at home.
Although I was tired, I went.
Why didn't you come?
Why are you sad?
I'll cook while you set the table.
Why didn't you come?

drills.answer: Estava a chover, por isso fiquei em casa.
drills.en: It was raining, so I stayed at home.
Although it's cold, I'm going to the beach.
drills.why: *Embora* takes the subjunctive (*esteja*); *apesar* de takes an infinitive.

drills.en: Even though it's cold, I'm going to the beach.
Why didn't you come?
drills.why: At the end of a question: *porquê*, with an accent.

drills.en: I'm hungry, so I'm going to eat.
drills.why: A result (so): *por isso*. *Porque* gives a reason.
